question: What term is used to describe the physical, touchable parts of a computer system?
explanation: Hardware refers specifically to the physical equipment of a computer that you can see and touch. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T2#BMP123_U1_T2_h1)

question: How do computer hardware and software depend on each other to function?

options.A: Software provides physical power while hardware stores the digital files
options.B: Hardware is only used for typing while software is used exclusively for printing
options.C: Software and hardware operate completely independently without any connection
options.D: Hardware needs software to run instructions, and software needs hardware to execute them

explanation: The physical machine needs programs to know what to do, and those programs need a physical home to run on. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T2#BMP123_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which part of the computer is commonly known as the brain of the system?
explanation: The CPU directs operations and carries out program instructions, much like a brain. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T2#BMP123_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is the primary function of the arithmetic logic unit inside a processor?

options.A: Storing permanent files when the computer turns off
options.B: Directing the physical flow of electrical power
options.C: Displaying high-resolution images on the monitor
options.D: Performing math calculations and logical decisions

explanation: The ALU is the specific sub-component within the CPU dedicated to mathematics and comparisons. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T2#BMP123_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT an input device?
explanation: A monitor displays information outward to the user, making it an output device rather than an input device. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T2#BMP123_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why would a busy clinic nurse or midwife use a barcode scanner during medication administration?

options.A: To permanently store large backups of hospital financial databases
options.B: To print physical paper prescriptions for the pharmacy department
options.C: To quickly and accurately enter patient data by reading wristbands
options.D: To increase the processing speed of the main computer processor

explanation: Scanners feed barcode data directly into the system as input, reducing manual typing errors. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T2#BMP123_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of an output device?

options.A: To convert digital computer data into a human-readable form
options.B: To send typed text and commands directly into the processor
options.C: To supply steady electrical voltage to internal computer chips
options.D: To store large amounts of data without needing electricity

explanation: Output devices translate machine code into visuals, sounds, or paper documents that humans can understand. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T2#BMP123_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which device would a midwife use to produce a physical paper copy of an antenatal clinic schedule?
explanation: A printer is an output device designed specifically to generate physical paper documents from digital files. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T2#BMP123_U1_T2_h4)

question: What happens to data stored in Random Access Memory when the computer is turned off?

options.D: It backs up to the cloud

explanation: RAM is volatile memory, meaning it requires electrical power to keep its data and loses everything upon shutdown. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T2#BMP123_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why is a Solid State Drive generally preferred over an older mechanical Hard Disk Drive in modern medical computers?

options.A: It relies entirely on temporary volatile power cells
options.B: It has no moving parts and operates much faster
options.C: It can only be read once before locking permanently
options.D: It requires manual disk cleaning every single week

explanation: SSDs use flash memory technology without spinning disks, making them faster and less prone to physical shock. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T2#BMP123_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary role of the motherboard in a computer system?

options.A: To convert digital text signals into printed paper pages
options.B: To permanently store large patient database records
options.C: To connect all internal components so they can communicate
options.D: To supply electrical voltage directly from wall sockets

explanation: The motherboard provides the electrical pathways and slots that link the CPU, RAM, and other hardware together. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T2#BMP123_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why are cooling fans and heat sinks necessary inside a desktop computer case?

options.A: To supply extra temporary RAM during heavy processing
options.B: To speed up the internet connection speed automatically
options.C: To prevent sensitive computer chips from overheating
options.D: To keep dust from entering the power supply unit

explanation: Processors generate significant heat while working, and cooling systems protect them from thermal damage. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T2#BMP123_U1_T2_h6)

question: What device should be used to protect sensitive hospital computers from sudden voltage spikes?
explanation: Surge protectors absorb unexpected electrical surges, protecting delicate internal computer hardware from damage. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T2#BMP123_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is the most practical first troubleshooting step if a desktop computer workstation fails to power on at all?

options.A: Check all power cable connections and wall socket power
options.B: Open the computer case and replace the main processor
options.C: Disconnect the keyboard and mouse to reset the display
options.D: Format the hard drive and reinstall the operating system

explanation: Checking basic power sources is the simplest and most logical first step before assuming major hardware failure. [learn more](BMP123_U1_T2#BMP123_U1_T2_h7)
